title: FsMount
description: Mount the shared JuiceFS volume at the owner's folder only (juicefs mount --subdir; juicefs-shared-storage design: one volume, a folder per user). Sent on the live link only to a daemon whose hello has fs_mount: after the welcome when the owner has a ready folder, and again when the folder or the credentials change (generation grows). Unreliable and never logged or stored: it carries the volume's credentials, which every node shares; the daemon must mount subdir and nothing else. The daemon mounts at its own data directory and answers with fs.status; a generation older than the one mounted is ignored.

volume.description: Volume name (the platform's one shared volume), also the mount directory name.

subdir.description: The owner's folder in the volume (users/<16 hex>): the only part of the volume the daemon mounts (juicefs mount --subdir).

generation.description: Grows when the owner's folder is provisioned again; a remount is due when it, the folder or the volume differs from the mounted one.

meta_url.description: Metadata engine URL without the password: postgres://juicefs@host:port/db?sslmode=...&search_path=juicefs. The volume's object storage keys live in its metadata (juicefs format).

client.description: The juicefs client to run: the daemon picks the asset of its platform (linux-amd64, linux-arm64, darwin-arm64…), downloads it and checks sha256, unless that exact version is already present. A tar.gz holding the juicefs binary.
